newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: France sends ministers to riot-torn Guiana.
newsitem.headline: France sends ministers to riot-torn Guiana.

text.p: Two French ministers arrived in French Guiana on Tuesday, days after organised gangs of armed rioters fought police, looted stores and set them on fire.

Local state-owned radio said Education Minister Francois Bayrou and Overseas Territories Minister Jean-Jacques de Peretti arrived early on Tuesday to discuss problems in the French department on the northeast coast of South America.

De Peretti has blamed the violence on failure by the previous Socialist government to increase the number of teachers in line with a population boom. Half of French Guiana's inhabitants are aged under 25.

Last week, one person died and at least 20 were injured during four nights of rioting in the capital Cayenne. The violence caused millions of dollars in damage to property -- mostly government buildings and shops.

The riots were sparked by a strike of high school students protesting at poor conditions in local schools, but these were soon overtaken by more radical groups, some of whom favour French Guiana's independence from mainland France.
De Peretti told parliament earlier this month that the students' demands were legitimate and that President Jacques Chirac had said they should be met.

Paris has sent more than 500 paramilitary riot police to the city of 35,000. French Guiana lags behind mainland France in housing, education and health. Official unemployment exceeds 23 percent and young people are the hardest hit.
